details: Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have intensified, leading to a significant downturn in cryptocurrency markets. A planned negotiation trip between the United States and Iran to Switzerland has been canceled, dampening hopes for de-escalation. Concurrently, Israeli missile strikes have continued in southern Lebanon, exacerbating regional instability. This series of events has triggered substantial long liquidations in the crypto market, pushing Bitcoin prices below $63,000.
title: Middle East Tensions Escalate as US-Iran Talks Canceled, Israel Strikes Lebanon

details: The Federal Reserve has adopted a more hawkish stance, impacting global currency markets and reducing expectations for interest rate cuts in 2026. Despite maintaining current rates, nine out of nineteen policymakers now anticipate a rate hike later this year. This shift is making U.S. dollar assets more appealing and has significantly decreased the likelihood of rate cuts this year, with an 81% market expectation of no cuts. Such a hawkish monetary policy typically strengthens the dollar and can exert pressure on equity markets, potentially leading to reduced liquidity for risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Federal Reserve's Hawkish Shift Pressures Global Currencies, Cuts Rate Cut Odds
